# Week of Sun 9 Mar 2025

## Reflection

<!-- [TEST-FIXTURE-PLACEHOLDER: weekly reflection prose for S027 test fixture] -->
You spent the first full week of Lent in London with the playhouse shut and the company's reckoning at the end of it. On Saturday morning you went up by water from Old Swan Stairs to the outer passage at Whitehall with Kemp and Richard Burbage, stood while the clerk trimmed his quills and read the three names on the warrant dated 15 March 1594, and walked the twenty pounds back by the Strand and Holborn.

At James Burbage's house in Holywell, Heminges set the sixteen angels, four sovereigns, and eight pounds of white money on the cloth and deducted five pounds in charges: sixteen shillings for the Greenwich boat-hire, thirty-four shillings in rewards to the hired men, boys, book-keeper, and tireman, and fifty shillings to the Cheapside mercer. The fifteen pounds remaining went into eight parts of thirty-seven shillings and sixpence, with the eighth part kept for the stock and eight shillings promised to Edith Kettlewood on Thursday.

Back at St Helen's you entered your thirty-seven shillings and sixpence as had in the Received column of the account book. You mean to put the share on a hired horse for Warwickshire in Lent.

## Memories

- 2025-03-15: Seven sharers took thirty-seven shillings and sixpence each, and the stock kept the eighth share.
